A1.justification: Both readable, complete 10-page PDFs describe the same MasqLoRA work and support comparison of the text, equations, tables and figures. Both end with references; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original backdoor experiments on SD v1.5 and SDXL 1.0, including performance comparisons, composability tests, ablations and semantic probing in Section 5.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experimental results in Tables 1–3 and Figures 4–6.

M1.justification: The contrastive embedding remapping, time-weighted diffusion loss, joint LoRA training and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Edits around the loss equations remove redundant inline symbols without altering the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same object and artistic-style backdoor tasks, data sources, six NSFW categories and module-composition scenarios. No represented data or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same BadT2I, Personalization, EvilEdit, Poisoned LoRA and benign reference rows. The semantic-probing comparison also retains the same base model, Benign LoRA and MasqLoRA participants.

E3.justification: The SD v1.5/SDXL 1.0 configurations, 30% poisoning rate, 5,000 benign and 5,000 triggered images per object target, evaluation metrics and ablation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Sections 5.4–5.6 retain the same module-stacking tests, sensitivity analyses for ranks, epochs and loss weights, and semantic-probing analysis. Table 3 and Figures 4–6 contain no added or removed analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions retain averaging across the three object-target experiments. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: The numerical entries, plotted results and qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports MasqLoRA ASR of 99.8% on SD v1.5 and 99.6% on SDXL 1.0 in both versions.

T1.justification: The optimization formulation, embedding constraint, loss definitions and SMI definition in Equations (1)–(6) are unchanged. Removing repeated loss symbols from introductory prose does not change the mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about a systematic LoRA backdoor framework, resolving semantic conflict, preserving benign functionality and achieving up to 99.8% ASR.

C2.justification: The explanations of semantic conflict, interference between stacked style modules, overtraining and excessive loss weighting are unchanged. The discussion of detection feasibility and potential semantic auditing is also retained.

D1.justification: Both versions disclose the same learning rates, dual-text-encoder handling, selected hyperparameters and evaluation procedures. The prospective code-release statement and repository address remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 47 works are cited, and the related-work discussion and novelty positioning are unchanged. Eight bibliography entries receive publication or metadata updates, rather than introducing different cited works.

P1.justification: v4 fixes sentence spacing and changes 'Lower FID are better' to 'Lower FID is better,' removes redundant inline loss symbols and updates bibliographic metadata. The section organization and narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Several labels in Figure 3 change from bold to regular type. Equation spacing and nearby text reflow slightly, and expanded references alter column and page breaks. No figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: v4 provides modest editorial and bibliographic improvements: reference [42] gains its venue, year and page range, several other entries gain publication details, and minor prose errors are fixed. These improve reference completeness and polish, while the scientific content, evidence and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
